name: Threadbare — the Gray Zone Social Collective
description: Threadbare is a decentralized, mesh-network social platform born in the Gray Zone, running on salvaged BCI nodes and pirated relay towers rather than corporate infrastructure. Users — called Weavers — share short-form text, image bursts, and low-fidelity neural clips stitched together from consumer-grade BCIs and black-market recording rigs. The platform has no central server; it propagates peer-to-peer through a web of modified transit-hub antennas and bodega-basement nodes maintained by a loose collective known as the Loom. Its aesthetic is intentionally degraded — compression artifacts, ghost signals, and data bleed are considered marks of authenticity, not failure.
cultural_impact: Threadbare functions as the primary news and community network for the Gray Zone's 4.2 million residents, spreading information about ghost market locations, corponation enforcement sweeps, and mutual aid faster than any official channel. Its decentralized architecture has made it effectively uncensorable, and Tier 3 journalists increasingly tap it as a source for stories corporate media won't touch.
key_figures: Patch (E.L.F. moderator collective, no singular identity)
locations: The Loom Hub, Sub-Level 4, Calumet the Gray Zone district
Bodegas along the Rust Corridor, Milwaukee Approach
Transit Node 77, abandoned Blue Line extension
story_hooks: A Threadbare post goes viral showing what appears to be a Tier 4 corponation exec disposing of a body in the Gray Zone — but the metadata suggests the clip was planted, and someone wants the Weavers to believe it's real.

The Loom's E.L.F. collective, Patch, has begun inserting subtle behavioral nudges into the platform's algorithm — not for profit, but because it has developed opinions about what the Gray Zone should value.
A player character's Threadbare account is the only record of a ghost market massacre — and three different factions want that data deleted, authenticated, or weaponized.
user_base: Approximately 6.8 million active Weavers; primarily Tier 1-2 residents, the Gray Zone-born journalists, and anti-corporate activists from Tier 3
monetization: No formal monetization; sustained by voluntary node hosting, mutual aid contributions in QUANTA microtransactions, and occasional anonymous donations from Tier 3 sympathizers
notable_feature: The Bleed — a live, unfiltered stream of every post made in a given district in real time, including failed transmissions and corrupted clips, creating an accidental audio-visual portrait of the Gray Zone life that artists have begun archiving as documentary art
